title: Hanuma's journey to Himalayas
introduction: After having been struck by Brahma's missile released by Indrajit, Rama and Lakshmana became unconscious. Sixty-seven crores of monkeys fainted. Hanuma and Vibhishana, however in consciousness, roared about in the battle-front with torches in their hands, making a search of Jambavan. They find Jambavan. Jambavan requests Hanuma to proceed to Himalayas, by crossing over the ocean and to bring four important herbs, viz. Mrita Sanjivani, Vishalya karani, Suvarna karani and Sandhani; so as to bring succour to the fainted army of monkeys. Hanuma begins his journey to Himalayas and reaches Mount Rishabha, where the wonderful herbs exist. Hanuma searches for the four wonderful herbs. But the herbs appear invisible for him. Hanuma uproots the mountain clothed with the four celestial herbs and carries it along with him. Inhaling the odour of those herbs, Rama, Lakshmana and all the monkeys regain their normal health.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 74th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
तयोस्तदा सादितयो रणाग्रे |
मुमोह सैन्यं हरियूथपानाम् |
सुग्रीवनीलाङ्गदजाम्बवन्तो |
न चापि किं चित्प्रतिपेदिरे ते
verses.iast:
tayostadā sāditayo raṇāgre |
mumoha sainyaṃ hariyUthapānām |
sugrīvanīlāñgadajāmbavanto |
na cāpi kiṃ citpratipedire te
verses.translation: Then, in the battle-front, Rama and Lakshmana were knocked down senseless. The army of monkey-leaders fainted. Sugreeva, Nila, Angada and Jambavan could not understand what to do.

glosses.meaning: even a little (of what to do).

verses.devanagari:
ततो विषण्णं समवेक्ष्य सैन्यं |
विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः |
उवाच शाखामृगराजवीरान् |
नाश्वासयन्नप्रतिमैर्वचोभिः
verses.iast:
tato viṣaṇṇaṃ samavekṣya sainyaṃ |
vibhīṣaṇo buddhimatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ |
uvāca śākhāmṛgarājavīrān |
nāśvāsayannapratimairvacobhiḥ
verses.translation: Seeing the entire army looking worried, Vibhishana, the best among the intelligent ones, spoke the following matchless words, consoling the warriors of Sugreeva, the lord of monkeys:

glosses.meaning: the warriors of Sugreeva the lord of monkeys

verses.devanagari:
मा भैष्ट नास्त्यत्र विषादकालो |
यदार्यपुत्राववशौ विषण्णौ |
स्वयम्भुवो वाक्यमथोद्वहन्तौ |
यत्सादिताविन्द्रजिदस्त्रजालैः
verses.iast:
mā bhaiṣṭa nāstyatra viṣādakālo |
yadāryaputrāvavaśau viṣaṇṇau |
svayambhuvo vākyamathodvahantau |
yatsāditāvindrajidastrajālaiḥ
verses.translation: "Honouring the spell sacred of Brahma the creator, the two sons of the venerable Dasaratha have actually lost their free will and became dejected and have allowed themselves to be knocked down by the missiles of Indrajit. Hence do not be afraid. There is no occasion for despondency now."

glosses.meaning: the two sons of venerable Dasaratha

verses.devanagari:
तस्मै तु दत्तं परमास्त्रमेतत् |
त्स्वयम्भुवा ब्राह्मममोघवेगम् |
तन्मानयन्तौ यदि राजपुत्रौ |
निपातितौ को अत्र विषादकालः
verses.iast:
tasmai tu dattaṃ paramāstrametat |
tsvayambhuvā brāhmamamoghavegam |
tanmānayantau yadi rājaputrau |
nipātitau ko atra viṣādakālaḥ
verses.translation: "This excellent missile, presided over by Brahma the creator, with never-failing strength, was given to Indrajit by Brahma. Honouring it, Rama and Lakshmana the princes fell down in battle. This not a time for despondency here."

glosses.meaning: excellent missile presided over by Brahma the creator amoghaviiryam = with never-failing strength

verses.devanagari:
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं तदा धीमान्मानयित्वा तु मारुतिः |
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हनूमांस्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
brāhmamastraṃ tadā dhīmānmānayitvā tu mārutiḥ |
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā hanUmāṃstamathābravīt
verses.translation: Then, the intelligent Hanuma, the son of wind-god, paying honour to the missile presided over by Brahma and hearing the words of Vibhishana, spoke the following words:

verses.devanagari:
अस्मिन्निहते सैन्ये वानराणां तरस्विनाम् |
यो यो धारयते प्राणांस्तं तमाश्वासयावहे
verses.iast:
asminnihate sainye vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām |
yo yo dhārayate prāṇāṃstaṃ tamāśvāsayāvahe
verses.translation: "Let us restore to confidence whosoever is in this army of energetic monkeys, after having been struck by the missile."

glosses.meaning: after having been struck by the missile

verses.devanagari:
तावुभौ युगपद्वीरौ हनूमद्राक्षसोत्तमौ |
उल्काहस्तौ तदा रात्रौ रणशीर्षे विचेरतुः
verses.iast:
tāvubhau yugapadvīrau hanUmadrākṣasottamau |
ulkāhastau tadā rātrau raṇaśīrṣe viceratuḥ
verses.translation: Both those valiant ones, Hanuma and Vibhishana, together at that time of the night, roamed about in the battle-front, with torches in their hands.

verses.devanagari:
भिन्नलाङ्गूलहस्तोरुपादाङ्गुलि शिरो धरैः |
स्रवद्भिः क्षतजं गात्रैः प्रस्रवद्भिः समन्ततः
पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसङ्कुलाम् |
शस्त्रैश्च पतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशाते वसुन्धराम्
verses.iast:
bhinnalāñgUlahastorupādāñguli śiro dharaiḥ |
sravadbhiḥ kṣatajaṃ gātraiḥ prasravadbhiḥ samantataḥ
patitaiḥ parvatākārairvānarairabhisañkulām |
śastraiśca patitairdīptairdadṛśāte vasundharām
verses.translation: Hanuma and Vibhishana saw the battle-field, covered on all sides, with mountain-sized monkeys fallen with heir tails, arms, thighs, feet, fingers and heaps of heads fractured with blood oozing from their limbs and urine flowing out. The earth was also covered with flaming weapons fallen around.

glosses.meaning: as also covered with flaming weapons.

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवमङ्गदं नीलं शरभं गन्धमादनम् |
गवाक्षम् च सिष्जेंणम् च वेगदर्शनमाहुकम्
मैन्दं नलं ज्योतिमुखं द्विविदं पनसं तथा |
विभीषणो हनूमांश्च ददृशाते हतान्रणे
verses.iast:
sugrīvamañgadaṃ nīlaṃ śarabhaṃ gandhamādanam |
gavākṣam ca siṣjeṃṇam ca vegadarśanamāhukam
maindaṃ nalaṃ jyotimukhaṃ dvividaṃ panasaṃ tathā |
vibhīṣaṇo hanUmāṃśca dadṛśāte hatānraṇe
verses.translation: Vibhishana and Hanuma saw Sugreeva, Angada, Nila, Sharabha, Gandhamadana, Gavaksha, Sushena, Vegadarshi, Mainda, Nala, Jyotimukha and a monkey called Dvivida, who were struck down on the battle-field.

verses.devanagari:
सप्तषष्टिर्हताः कोट्यो वानराणां तरस्विनाम् |
अह्नः पञ्चमशेषेण वल्लभेन स्वयम्भुवः
verses.iast:
saptaṣaṣṭirhatāḥ koṭyo vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām |
ahnaḥ pañcamaśeṣeṇa vallabhena svayambhuvaḥ
verses.translation: Sixty seven crores of powerful monkeys were struck down by the cherished missile of Brahma, the self-born creator, in the fifth and last period* of the day.
notes: *The twelve hours of the day were commonly divided into five parts consisting of six Ghatikas (or two hours and twenty four minutes) each. They were known by the names of PraataH (early morning), Sangava (forenoon), Madhyaahva (midday), Aparaahna (afternoon) and Saayaahna (evening).

glosses.meaning: in the fifth and last period* of the day.

verses.devanagari:
सागरौघनिभं भीमं दृष्ट्वा बाणार्दितं बलम् |
मार्गते जाम्बवन्तं स्म हनूमान्सविभीषणः
verses.iast:
sāgaraughanibhaṃ bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇārditaṃ balam |
mārgate jāmbavantaṃ sma hanUmānsavibhīṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Hanuma, along with Vibhishana, began to search for Jambavan, while looking at the terrific army (wounded by the arrows) which appeared like the tide of an ocean.

glosses.meaning: while looking at bhiimam balam = the terrific army
and appearing like a tide of an ocean.

verses.devanagari:
स्वभावजरया युक्तं वृद्धं शरशतैश् चितम् |
प्रजापतिसुतं वीरं शाम्यन्तमिव पावकम्
दृष्ट्वा तमुपसङ्गम्य पौलस्त्यो वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
svabhāvajarayā yuktaṃ vṛddhaṃ śaraśataiś citam |
prajāpatisutaṃ vīraṃ śāmyantamiva pāvakam
dṛṣṭvā tamupasañgamya paulastyo vākyamabravīt |
verses.translation: Looking at Jambavan, the son of Brahma, who was naturally bequeathed with old age, an elderly person, with his body conspicuous of hundreds of arrows and a valiant person looking like an extinguishing fire, Vibhishana approached him and spoke as follows:

glosses.meaning: and a valiant with hundreds of arrows

verses.devanagari:
कच्चिदार्यशरैस्तीर्ष्णैर्न प्राणा ध्वंसितास्तव
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गवः |
कृच्छ्रादभ्युद्गिरन्वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
kaccidāryaśaraistīrṣṇairna prāṇā dhvaṃsitāstava
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavānṛkṣapuñgavaḥ |
kṛcchrādabhyudgiranvākyamidaṃ vacanamabravīt

verses.devanagari:
नैरृतेन्द्रमहावीर्यस्वरेण त्वाभिलक्षये |
विद्धगात्रः शितैर्बाणैर्न त्वां पश्यामि चक्षुषा
verses.iast:
nairṛtendramahāvīryasvareṇa tvābhilakṣaye |
viddhagātraḥ śitairbāṇairna tvāṃ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā
verses.translation: "O Vibhishana, the leader of demons, with a great prowess! I am able to recognize you by your voice alone. Pierced with sharp arrows, I am not able to see you with my eyes."

verses.devanagari:
अञ्जना सुप्रजा येन मातरिश्वा च नैरृत |
हनूमान्वानरश्रेष्ठः प्राणान्धारयते क्व चित्
verses.iast:
añjanā suprajā yena mātariśvā ca nairṛta |
hanUmānvānaraśreṣṭhaḥ prāṇāndhārayate kva cit
verses.translation: "O Vibhishana, of good manners! Does Hanuma, the foremost among monkeys, because of whom, Anjana (his mother) and the wind-god are his blessed parents survive, holding his life any where nearby?"

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यमुवाचेदं विभीषणः |
आर्यपुत्रावतिक्रम्य कस्मात्पृच्छसि मारुतिम्
verses.iast:
śrutvā jāmbavato vākyamuvācedaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ |
āryaputrāvatikramya kasmātpṛcchasi mārutim
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Jambavana, Vibhishana spoke the following words, "why do you enquire about Hanuman, passing over the venerable sons of Dasaratha?"

verses.devanagari:
नैव राजनि सुग्रीवे नाङ्गदे नापि राघवे |
आर्य सन्दर्शितः स्नेहो यथा वायुसुते परः
verses.iast:
naiva rājani sugrīve nāñgade nāpi rāghave |
ārya sandarśitaḥ sneho yathā vāyusute paraḥ
verses.translation: "O venerable one! The exceptional affection, you are showing towards Hanuma, is not being shown towards Sugreeva or Angada or even Rama."

verses.devanagari:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवान्वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
शृणु नैरृतशार्दूल यस्मात्पृच्छामि मारुतिम्
verses.iast:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavānvākyamabravīt |
śṛṇu nairṛtaśārdUla yasmātpṛcchāmi mārutim
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Vibhishana, Jambavan replied as follows: "O the foremost among demons! Listen to me, why I am enquiring about Hanuma."

verses.devanagari:
अस्मिञ्जीवति वीरे तु हतमप्यहतं बलम् |
हनूमत्युज्झितप्राणे जीवन्तोऽपि मृता वयम्
verses.iast:
asmiñjīvati vīre tu hatamapyahataṃ balam |
hanUmatyujjhitaprāṇe jīvanto'pi mṛtā vayam
verses.translation: "If that brave Hanuma is surviving, the whole army even if killed, is unhurt. On the other hand, if Hanuma has given up is life, we are all dead, even though living."

verses.devanagari:
ध्रियते मारुतिस्तात मारुतप्रतिमो यदि |
वैश्वानरसमो वीर्ये जीविताशा ततो भवेत्
verses.iast:
dhriyate mārutistāta mārutapratimo yadi |
vaiśvānarasamo vīrye jīvitāśā tato bhavet
verses.translation: "O dear child! If Hanuma, who is equal to the wind and the fire in prowess, survives; then there is a hope for all of us to survive.'

glosses.meaning: there is a hope to live (for us).

verses.devanagari:
ततो वृद्धमुपागम्य नियमेनाभ्यवादयत् |
गृह्य जाम्बवतः पादौ हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.iast:
tato vṛddhamupāgamya niyamenābhyavādayat |
gṛhya jāmbavataḥ pādau hanUmānmārutātmajaḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, Hanuma the son of wind-god approaching the elderly Jambavan, offered his salutation, by grasping the feet of Jambavan with modesty.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं तथापि व्यथितेन्द्रियः |
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं स मेने ऋक्षपुङ्गवः
verses.iast:
śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ tathāpi vyathitendriyaḥ |
punarjātamivātmānaṃ sa mene ṛkṣapuñgavaḥ
verses.translation: Hearing the voice of Hanuma, Jambavan, the foremost among monkeys, with perturbed senses, considered himself as though born again.

verses.devanagari:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमन्तं स जाम्बवान् |
आगच्छ हरिशार्दूलवानरांस्त्रातुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
tato'bravīnmahātejā hanUmantaṃ sa jāmbavān |
āgaccha hariśārdUlavānarāṃstrātumarhasi
verses.translation: Thereafter, that Jambavan of great splendour spoke to Hanuma as follows: "Come on, O foremost of monkeys! You ought to protect the lives of monkeys."

verses.devanagari:
नान्यो विक्रमपर्याप्तस्त्वमेषां परमः सखा |
त्वत्पराक्रमकालोऽयं नान्यं पश्यामि कञ् चन
verses.iast:
nānyo vikramaparyāptastvameṣāṃ paramaḥ sakhā |
tvatparākramakālo'yaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmi kañ cana
verses.translation: "You are the great companion for these monkeys, by your copious prowess. There is no other person. This is the appropriate time to show your prowess. I do not see any other person to do it."

glosses.meaning: is the time to show your prowess

verses.devanagari:
ऋक्षवानरवीराणामनीकानि प्रहर्षय |
विशल्यौ कुरु चाप्येतौ सादितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.iast:
ṛkṣavānaravīrāṇāmanīkāni praharṣaya |
viśalyau kuru cāpyetau sāditau rāmalakṣmaṇau
verses.translation: "Cheer up the martial warriors of both monkeys and bears. Heal Rama and Lakshmana from their arrow-wounds."

verses.devanagari:
गत्वा परममध्वानमुपर्युपरि सागरम् |
हिमवन्तं नगश्रेष्ठं हनूमन्गन्तुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
gatvā paramamadhvānamuparyupari sāgaram |
himavantaṃ nagaśreṣṭhaṃ hanUmangantumarhasi
verses.translation: "O Hanuma! You ought to go to Himalaya, the foremost of mountains, by traveling higher and higher over the large ocean."

verses.devanagari:
ततः काञ्चनमत्युग्रमृषभं पर्वतोत्तमम् |
कैलासशिखरं चापि द्रक्ष्यस्यरिनिषूदन
verses.iast:
tataḥ kāñcanamatyugramṛṣabhaṃ parvatottamam |
kailāsaśikharaṃ cāpi drakṣyasyariniṣUdana
verses.translation: "O annihilator of enemies! Thereafter, you will see there the Mount Rishabha, the excellent mountain and the very much powerful peak of Kailasa, with a golden hue."

verses.devanagari:
तयोः शिखरयोर्मध्ये प्रदीप्तमतुलप्रभम् |
सर्वौषधियुतं वीर द्रक्ष्यस्यौषधिपर्वतम्
verses.iast:
tayoḥ śikharayormadhye pradīptamatulaprabham |
sarvauṣadhiyutaṃ vīra drakṣyasyauṣadhiparvatam
verses.translation: "O valiant Hanuma! In the midst of these two peaks, you will see a blazing and unequally brilliant herbal mountain, containing all kinds of herbs."

verses.devanagari:
तस्य वानरशार्दूलचतस्रो मूर्ध्नि सम्भवाः |
द्रक्ष्यस्योषधयो दीप्ता दीपयन्त्यो दिशो दश
verses.iast:
tasya vānaraśārdUlacatasro mUrdhni sambhavāḥ |
drakṣyasyoṣadhayo dīptā dīpayantyo diśo daśa
verses.translation: "O foremost of monkeys! Sprouted on the head of that mountain, are four blazing herbs. You can see them, illuminating the ten quarters."

glosses.meaning: on the head of that mountain

verses.devanagari:
मृतसञ्जीवनीं चैव विशल्यकरणीम् अपि |
सौवर्णकरणीं चैव सन्धानीं च महौषधीम्
verses.iast:
mṛtasañjīvanīṃ caiva viśalyakaraṇīm api |
sauvarṇakaraṇīṃ caiva sandhānīṃ ca mahauṣadhīm
verses.translation: "You can see there, Mrita Sanjivani (capable of restoring the dead to life), Vishalyakarani (capable of extracting weapons and healing all wounds inflicted by weapons), Suvarnakarani (restoring the body to its original complexion) and Sandhani, the great herb (capable of joining severed limbs or fractured bone)."

glosses.meaning: (you can see) Mrita sanjiivani (capable of restoring the dead to life) and also
Vishalyakarani (capable of extracting weapons and healing all wounds inflicted by weapons)
Suvarna karani (restoring the body to its original complexion)
and sandhani (capable of joining severed limbs or fractured bones)

verses.devanagari:
ताः सर्वा हनुमन्गृह्य क्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि |
आश्वासय हरीन्प्राणैर्योज्य गन्धवहात्मजः
verses.iast:
tāḥ sarvā hanumangṛhya kṣipramāgantumarhasi |
āśvāsaya harīnprāṇairyojya gandhavahātmajaḥ
verses.translation: "O Hanuma! Bring all those herbs quickly. O son of wind-god! Bring succour to the monkeys, by injecting lives into them."

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यं हनूमान्हरिपुङ्गवः |
आपूर्यत बलोद्धर्षैस्तोयवेगैरिवार्णवः
verses.iast:
śrutvā jāmbavato vākyaṃ hanUmānharipuñgavaḥ |
āpUryata baloddharṣaistoyavegairivārṇavaḥ
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Jambavan, Hanuma the son of wind-god was infused with animated strength, as the ocean gets animated with the force of the wind.

glosses.meaning: elevates with the force of the wind.

verses.devanagari:
स पर्वततटाग्रस्थः पीडयन्पर्वतोत्तरम् |
हनूमान्दृश्यते वीरो द्वितीय इव पर्वतः
verses.iast:
sa parvatataṭāgrasthaḥ pīḍayanparvatottaram |
hanūmāndṛśyate vīro dvitīya iva parvataḥ
verses.translation: Standing on the summit of Trikuta mountain and pressing the foremost of mountains (with his feet), that valiant Hanuma appeared like a second mountain.

glosses.meaning: standing on the summit of Trikuta mountain

verses.devanagari:
हरिपादविनिर्भिन्नो निषसाद स पर्वतः |
न शशाक तदात्मानं सोढुं भृशनिपीडितः
verses.iast:
haripādavinirbhinno niṣasāda sa parvataḥ |
na śaśāka tadātmānaṃ soḍhuṃ bhṛśanipīḍitaḥ
verses.translation: Then, increasingly pressed and bent by Hanuma's feet, that mountain was not able to bear its weight and sank.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य पेतुर्नगा भूमौ हरिवेगाच्च जज्वलुः |
शृङ्गाणि च व्यकीर्यन्त पीडितस्य हनूमता
verses.iast:
tasya peturnagā bhUmau harivegācca jajvaluḥ |
śṛñgāṇi ca vyakīryanta pīḍitasya hanUmatā
verses.translation: The trees on that mountain, pressed by Hanuma, fell to the ground and caught fire due to rapidity of Hanuma. Its peaks also got broken.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिन्सम्पीड्यमाने तु भग्नद्रुमशिलातले |
न शेकुर्वानराः स्थातुं घूर्णमाने नगोत्तमे
verses.iast:
tasminsampīḍyamāne tu bhagnadrumaśilātale |
na śekurvānarāḥ sthātuṃ ghUrṇamāne nagottame
verses.translation: The monkeys were unable to stand on that excellent mountain, which started to reel, while being pressed severely by Hanuma, as the trees standing on it and the rocks got broken.

glosses.meaning: as the trees standing on it and the rocks got broken.

verses.devanagari:
स घूर्णितमहाद्वारा प्रभग्नगृहगोपुरा |
लङ्का त्रासाकुला रात्रौ प्रनृत्तेवाभवत्तदा
verses.iast:
sa ghUrṇitamahādvārā prabhagnagṛhagopurā |
lañkā trāsākulā rātrau pranṛttevābhavattadā
verses.translation: Confounded with panic, the City of Lanka, whose principal gates were broken, whose houses and town-gates were shattered, appeared as though dancing at night.

glosses.meaning: whose houses and town-gates were shattered

verses.devanagari:
पृथिवीधरसङ्काशो निपीड्य धरणीधरम् |
पृथिवीं क्षोभयामास सार्णवां मारुतात्मजः
verses.iast:
pṛthivīdharasañkāśo nipīḍya dharaṇīdharam |
pṛthivīṃ kṣobhayāmāsa sārṇavāṃ mārutātmajaḥ
verses.translation: Pressing hard the mountain, Hanuma equal to a mountain, caused the earth along with the ocean to shake.

glosses.meaning: caused the earth along with the ocean to shake.

verses.devanagari:
आरुरोह तदा तस्माद्धरिर्मलयपर्वतम् |
मेरुमन्दरसंकाशं नानाप्रस्रवणाकुलम्
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णम् विकासिकमलोत्पलम् |
सेवितम् देवगन्धर्वैः षष्टियोजनमुच्छ्रितम्
विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् |
नानामृगगणाकीर्णम् बहुकन्दरशोभितम्
सर्वानाकुलयंस्तत्र यक्षगन्धर्वकिम्नरान् |
हनुमान् मेघसम्काशो ववृधे मारुतात्मजः
verses.iast:
āruroha tadā tasmāddharirmalayaparvatam |
merumandarasaṅkāśaṃ nānāprasravaṇākulam
nānādrumalatākīrṇam vikāsikamalotpalam |
sevitam devagandharvaiḥ ṣaṣṭiyojanamucchritam
vidyādharairmunigaṇairapsarobhirniṣevitam |
nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇam bahukandaraśobhitam
sarvānākulayaṃstatra yakṣagandharvakimnarān |
hanumān meghasamkāśo vavṛdhe mārutātmajaḥ
verses.translation: From that mountain, Hanuma then ascended Mount Malaya, appearing as Mounts Meru and Mandara, filled with several kinds of cascades, full of many trees and creepers, having Kamala and Utpala lotuses blooming, visited by celestials and celestial musicians, having a height of sixty Yojanas (four hundred eighty miles), frequented by Vidyodharas, a number of sages and Apsaras the nymphs, filled with various kinds of animal-troupes and illuminated by many caves, Hanuma grew his body, appearing like a cloud, bewildering Yakshas, Gandharvas and Kinnaras.

glosses.meaning: appearing like Mounts Meru and Manadara
filled with several kinds of cascades
full of many trees and creepers
having Kamala and utpala lotuses blooming
having a height of sixty Yojanas
filled with various kinds of animate troupes

verses.devanagari:
पद्भ्यां तु शैलमापीड्य वडवामुखवन्मुखम् |
विवृत्योग्रं ननादोच्चैस्त्रासयन्निव राक्षसान्
verses.iast:
padbhyāṃ tu śailamāpīḍya vaḍavāmukhavanmukham |
vivṛtyograṃ nanādoccaistrāsayanniva rākṣasān
verses.translation: Pressing the mountain hard with his feet, opening his terrific mouth which shone like a submarine fire and frightening the demons, Hanuma roared loudly.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य नानद्यमानस्य श्रुत्वा निनदमद्भुतम् |
लङ्कास्था राक्षसाः सर्वे न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं भयात्
verses.iast:
tasya nānadyamānasya śrutvā ninadamadbhutam |
lañkāsthā rākṣasāḥ sarve na śekuḥ spandituṃ bhayāt
verses.translation: Hearing his loud noise, roaring clamorously, the foremost of demons residing in the City of Lanka, were not able to stir anywhere.

verses.devanagari:
नमस्कृत्वाथ रामाय मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः |
राघवार्थे परं कर्म समैहत परन्तपः
verses.iast:
namaskṛtvātha rāmāya mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ |
rāghavārthe paraṃ karma samaihata parantapaḥ
verses.translation: Hanuma of terrific prowess, annihilator of his enemies, after offering salutation to the ocean, made up his mind to embark on a prime act for the sake of Rama.

verses.devanagari:
स पुच्छमुद्यम्य भुजङ्गकल्पं |
विनम्य पृष्ठं श्रवणे निकुञ्च्य |
विवृत्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभम् |
आपुप्लुवे व्योम्नि स चण्डवेगः
verses.iast:
sa pucchamudyamya bhujañgakalpaṃ |
vinamya pṛṣṭhaṃ śravaṇe nikuñcya |
vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābham |
āpupluve vyomni sa caṇḍavegaḥ
verses.translation: Raising his tail which resembled on serpent, bending his back, contracting his ears and opening his month which shone like a terrific submarines-fire, Hanuma jumped into the sky, with a head long speed.

glosses.meaning: which shore like a terrific submarine fire

verses.devanagari:
स वृक्षषण्डांस्तरसा जहार |
शैलाञ्शिलाः प्राकृतवानरांश् च |
बाहूरुवेगोद्धतसम्प्रणुन्नास् |
स्ते क्षीणवेगाः सलिले निपेतुः
verses.iast:
sa vṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃstarasā jahāra |
śailāñśilāḥ prākṛtavānarāṃś ca |
bāhūruvegoddhatasampraṇunnās |
ste kṣīṇavegāḥ salile nipetuḥ
verses.translation: By his velocity, he carried away a multitude of trees, mountains and some ordinary monkeys. Driven up and away by the momentum generated from his arms and thighs, they fell down in water when their speed diminished.

glosses.meaning: and driven up and away by the momentum generated from his arms and thighs

verses.devanagari:
स तौ प्रसार्योरगभोगकल्पौ |
भुजौ भुजङ्गारिनिकाशवीर्यः |
जगाम मेरुं नगराजमग्र्यं |
दिशः प्रकर्षन्निव वायुसूनुः
verses.iast:
sa tau prasāryoragabhogakalpau |
bhujau bhujañgārinikāśavīryaḥ |
jagāma meruṃ nagarājamagryaṃ |
diśaḥ prakarṣanniva vāyusūnuḥ
verses.translation: Stretching his arms, looking like coils of serpents, that Hanuma vying with the prowess of hostile Garuda the eagle, headed towards the excellent mountain of Himalayas, with gush as though he was drawing away the four quarters.

glosses.meaning: vying with the prowess of hostile Garuda the eagle
as though he was drawing forth

verses.devanagari:
स सागरं घूर्णितवीचिमालं
तथा भृशं भ्रामितसर्वसत्त्वम् |
समीक्षमाणः सहसा जगाम
चक्रं यथा विष्णुकराग्रमुक्तम्
verses.iast:
sa sāgaraṃ ghUrṇitavīcimālaṃ
tathā bhṛśaṃ bhrāmitasarvasattvam |
samīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā jagāma
cakraṃ yathā viṣṇukarāgramuktam
verses.translation: Beholding the sea, whose waves along with its water were made to agitate and all whose creatures were caused to whirl round, Hanuma quickly speeded up, like the discuss loosed by the fingers of Lord Vishnu.

glosses.meaning: whose waves along with its water were made to agitate bhraamita sarvasaattvam = and all whose creatures were caused to whirl round
loosed by the fingers of Lord Vishnu.

verses.devanagari:
स पर्वतान्वृक्षगणान्सरांसि |
नदीस्तटाकानि पुरोत्तमानि |
स्फीताञ्जनांस्तानपि सम्प्रपश्यञ् |
जगाम वेगात्पितृतुल्यवेगः
verses.iast:
sa parvatānvṛkṣagaṇānsarāṃsi |
nadīstaṭākāni purottamāni |
sphītāñjanāṃstānapi samprapaśyañ |
jagāma vegātpitṛtulyavegaḥ
verses.translation: Gazing at the hills, flocks of birds, lakes, rivers, pools and excellent towns full of people, that Hanuma with a speed equal to that of the wind-god his father, shot forth towards Himalayas.

glosses.meaning: with a speed equal to the wind-god

verses.devanagari:
आदित्यपथमाश्रित्य जगाम स गतश्रमः |
हनुमांस्त्वरितो वीरः पितुस्तुल्यपराक्रमः
verses.iast:
ādityapathamāśritya jagāma sa gataśramaḥ |
hanumāṃstvarito vīraḥ pitustulyaparākramaḥ
verses.translation: That valiant Hanuma, with a prowess equal to that of his father, whose fatigue was gone, swiftly rushed, taking recourse to the orbit of the sun.

glosses.meaning: with a prowess equal to that of his father
to the orbit of the sun.

verses.devanagari:
जवेन महता युक्तो मारुतिर्मारुतो यथा |
जगाम हरिशार्दूलो दिशः शब्देन नादयन्
verses.iast:
javena mahatā yukto mārutirmāruto yathā |
jagāma hariśārdūlo diśaḥ śabdena nādayan
verses.translation: With a great speed of wind, reverberating the four quarters with sound, Hanuma the foremost of monkeys, hastened towards Himalayas.

verses.devanagari:
स्मर्न् जाम्बवतो वाक्यम् मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः |
ददर्श सहसा चापि हिमवन्तं महाकपिः
verses.iast:
smarn jāmbavato vākyam mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ |
dadarśa sahasā cāpi himavantaṃ mahākapiḥ
verses.translation: Remembering the words of Jambavan, Hanuma the great monkey with a terrific stride, suddenly saw Mount Himalaya too.

verses.devanagari:
नानाप्रस्रवणोपेतं बहुकन्दरनिर्झरम् |
श्वेताभ्रचयसङ्काशैः शिखरैश्चारुदर्शनैः
शोभितं विविधैर्वृक्तैरगमत्पर्वतोत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
nānāprasravaṇopetaṃ bahukandaranirjharam |
śvetābhracayasañkāśaiḥ śikharaiścārudarśanaiḥ
śobhitaṃ vividhairvṛktairagamatparvatottamam |
verses.translation: Hanuma went to Mount Himalaya, the foremost of mountains, embellished with various kinds of cascades, many kinds of caves, mountain-streams and summits resembling an assemblage of white clouds as also many kinds of trees.

glosses.meaning: resembling an assemblage of white clouds

verses.devanagari:
स तम् समासाद्य महानगेन्द्रम् |
मतिप्रवृद्धोत्तमघोरशृङ्गम् |
ददर्श पुण्यानि महाश्रमाणि |
सुरर्षिसङ्घोत्तमसेवितानि
verses.iast:
sa tam samāsādya mahānagendram |
matipravṛddhottamaghoraśṛñgam |
dadarśa puṇyāni mahāśramāṇi |
surarṣisañghottamasevitAni
verses.translation: Having approached that great mountain having excellent overbearing summits, he saw great holy hermitages, inhabited by a multitude of divine sages.

glosses.meaning: that great mountain ati pravR^iddhottmahomashR^iN^gam = with excellent overbearing golden summits
inhabited by a multitude of divine sages.

verses.devanagari:
स ब्रह्मकोशं रजतालयं च |
शक्रालयं रुद्रशरप्रमोक्षम् |
हयाननं ब्रह्मशिरश्च दीप्तं |
ददर्श वैवस्वत किङ्करांश् च
verses.iast:
sa brahmakośaṃ rajatālayaṃ ca |
śakrālayaṃ rudraśarapramokṣam |
hayānanaṃ brahmaśiraśca dīptaṃ |
dadarśa vaivasvata kiñkarAṃś ca
verses.translation: He saw the abode of Brahma the lord of creation, Kailasa the abode of Shiva the lord of dissolution, the abode of Indra the lord of celestials, the arrow-discharging place of Rudra, the worshipping place of Hayagriva, the horse-faced form of Vishnu, the shining place at which Brahma's head fell down, the sun-god and Kimkaras.

glosses.meaning: the abode of Brahma the lord of creation
Kailasa the abode of Shiva the lord of dissolution
the abode of Indra the lord of celestials
arrow-discharging place of Rudra (a figure of half-male and half-female born from Brhama's forehead)
place at which Brahma's head fell down

verses.devanagari:
वज्रालयं वैश्वरणालयं च |
सूर्यप्रभं सूर्यनिबन्धनं च |
ब्रह्मासनं शङ्करकार्मुकं च |
ददर्श नाभिं च वसुन्धरायाः
verses.iast:
vajrālayaṃ vaiśvaraṇālayaṃ ca |
sūryaprabhaṃ sūryanibandhanaṃ ca |
brahmāsanaṃ śañkarakārmukaṃ ca |
dadarśa nAbhiṃ ca vasundharAyAḥ
verses.translation: He saw the abode of Agni the fire-god, the abode of Kubera (son of Visrava) shining like the sun, the spot where the sun was tied down, the abode of Brahma, the abode of bow belonging to Lord Shiva and the novel of the earth (containing the hole through which one can enter Patala the nethermost subterranean region).

glosses.meaning: the abode of Kubera (son of sage Visrava)
the spot where the sun was tied down (for being scrapped by Viswakarma
the abode of bow belonging to Lord Shiva vasundharaayaaH naabhimcha = and the novel of the earth (containing the hole through which one can enter Patala the nethermost subterranean region).

verses.devanagari:
कैलासमग्र्यं हिमवच्छिलां च |
तथर्षभं काञ्चनशैलमग्र्यम् |
स दीप्तसर्वौषधिसम्प्रदीप्तं |
ददर्श सर्वौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रम्
verses.iast:
kailāsamagryaṃ himavacchilāṃ ca |
tatharṣabhaṃ kāñcanaśailamagryam |
sa dīptasarvauṣadhisampradīptaṃ |
dadarśa sarvauṣadhiparvatendram
verses.translation: He saw the gigantic Mount Kailasa, the rock of Mount Himalaya (on which Lord Shiva is believed to have practiced austerities and abstract meditation) and Mount Rishabha, the lofty golden mountain, which was highly illumined by the flaming herbs and the lord of mountains on which all types of herbs grew.

glosses.meaning: the rock of Mount Himalaya (on which Lord Shiva is believed to have practiced austerities and abstract meditation)
which was highly illumined by the flaming herbs
the lord of mountains on which all herbs grew.

verses.devanagari:
स तं समीक्ष्यानलरश्मिदीप्तं |
विसिष्मिये वासवदूतसूनुः |
आप्लुत्य तं चौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रं |
तत्रौषधीनां विचयं चकार
verses.iast:
sa taṃ samīkṣyānalaraśmidīptaṃ |
visiṣmiye vāsavadūtasūnuḥ |
āplutya taṃ cauṣadhiparvatendraṃ |
tatrauṣadhīnāṃ vicayaṃ cakāra
verses.translation: Seeing that mountain shining with a heap of fire, Hanuma the son of wind-god, who is the envoy of Indra, was surprised to see that great mountain of herbs and then made a search for the herbs.

glosses.meaning: shining with a heap of fire
on that great mountain of herbs

verses.devanagari:
स योजनसहस्राणि समतीत्य महाकपिः |
दिव्यौषधिधरं शैलं व्यचरन्मारुतात्मजः
verses.iast:
sa yojanasahasrAṇi samatītya mahākapiḥ |
divyauṣadhidharaṃ śailaṃ vyacaranmārutātmajaḥ
verses.translation: That Hanuma, the great monkey, having crossed thousands of yojanas, walked around that mountain, searching for the heavenly herbs.

verses.devanagari:
महौषध्यस्तु ताः सर्वास्तस्मिन्पर्वतसत्तमे |
विज्ञायार्थिनमायान्तं ततो जग्मुरदर्शनम्
verses.iast:
mahauṣadhyastu tāḥ sarvāstasminparvatasattame |
viGYAyArthinamAyAntaṃ tato jagmuradarśanam
verses.translation: Knowing then that somebody was coming in search of them, all the distinguished herbs on that mountain disappeared from Hanuma's view.

verses.devanagari:
स ता महात्मा हनुमान पश्यं |
शुकोप कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद |
अमृष्यमाणोऽग्निनिकाशचक्षुर् |
र्महीधरेन्द्रं तमुवाच वाक्यम्
verses.iast:
sa tā mahātmā hanumāna paśyaṃ |
śukopa kopācca bhṛśaṃ nanāda |
amṛṣyamāṇo'gninikāśacakṣur |
rmahīdharendraṃ tamuvāca vākyam
verses.translation: In not seeing them thus, that great souled Hanuma was enraged. He made a loud noise in anger unable to bear it, Hanuma with his eyes as red as the fire, spoke the following words to the prince of mountains.

glosses.meaning: with his eyes as red as the fire

verses.devanagari:
किमेतदेवं सुविनिश्चितं ते |
यद्राघवे नासि कृतानुकम्पः |
पश्याद्य मद्बाहुबलाभिभूतो
विकीर्णमात्मानमथो नगेन्द्र
verses.iast:
kimetadevaṃ suviniścitaṃ te |
yadrāghave nāsi kṛtānukampaḥ |
paśyādya madbāhubalābhibhūto
vikīrṇamātmānamatho nagendra
verses.translation: "O prince of mountains! Is it quite sure that you have not shown any compassion for Rama? If it is so, overcome by the strength of my arms; find yourself shattered to pieces today."

glosses.meaning: that you have not shown any compassion
for Rama?' atho = If it is so
overcome by the strength of my arms

verses.devanagari:
स तस्य शृङ्गं सनगं सनागं |
सकाञ्चनं धातुसहस्रजुष्टम् |
विकीर्णकूटं चलिताग्रसानुं
प्रगृह्य वेगात्सहसोन्ममाथ
verses.iast:
sa tasya śṛñgaṃ sanagaṃ sanāgaṃ |
sakāñcanaṃ dhātusahasrajuṣṭam |
vikīrṇakūṭaṃ calitāgrasānuṃ
pragṛhya vegātsahasonmamātha
verses.translation: Fiercely seizing hold of the top of that mountain, furnished with thousands of minerals, with its trees, elephants and gold, with the projections of mountain shattered and the crest of its plateau set on fire, at once sprang up with speed.

glosses.meaning: with the projections of mountain shattered
and the crest of its plateau set on fire

verses.devanagari:
स तं समुत्पाट्य खमुत्पपात |
वित्रास्य लोकान्ससुरान्सुरेन्द्रान् |
संस्तूयमानः खचरैरनेकैर् |
जगाम वेगाद्गरुडोग्रवीर्यः
verses.iast:
sa taṃ samutpāṭya khamutpapāta |
vitrāsya lokānsasurānsurendrān |
saṃstūyamānaḥ khacarairanekair |
jagāma vegādgaruḍogravīryaḥ
verses.translation: Having uprooted that mountain, frightening the worlds together with the leaders of celestials and demons inhabiting them and being praised by many aerial beings, Hanuma sprang up into the sky and proceeded expeditiously with the terrible speed of Garuda the eagle.

glosses.meaning: including the leaders of celestials and demons inhabiting them samstunyamaanah = and being praised
with the terrible speed of Garuda the eagle.

verses.devanagari:
स भास्कराध्वानमनुप्रपन्नस् |
तद्भास्कराभं शिखरं प्रगृह्य |
बभौ तदा भास्करसंनिकाशो |
रवेः समीपे प्रतिभास्कराभः
verses.iast:
sa bhāskarādhvānamanuprapannas |
tadbhāskarābhaṃ śikharaṃ pragṛhya |
babhau tadā bhāskarasaṃnikāśo |
raveḥ samīpe pratibhāskarābhaḥ
verses.translation: Grasping that mountain-peak, radiant as the sun, that Hanuma who resembled the sun, having reached the orbit of the sun, shone as a second sun (as sun's image) in the vicinity of the sun.

verses.devanagari:
स तेन शैलेन भृशं रराज |
शैलोपमो गन्धवहात्मजस्तु |
सहस्रधारेण सपावकेन |
चक्रेण खे विष्णुरिवार्पितेन
verses.iast:
sa tena śailena bhṛśaṃ rarāja |
śailopamo gandhavahātmajastu |
sahasradhāreṇa sapāvakena |
cakreṇa khe viṣṇurivārpitena
verses.translation: In the sky, with that mountain in his hand, that Hanuma the offspring of the wind-god, who resembled a mountain himself, appeared mostly like Vishnu with his flaming discuss with its thousand edges holding his hand.

glosses.meaning: that Hanuma the offspring of the wind-god

verses.devanagari:
तं वानराः प्रेक्ष्य तदा विनेदुः |
स तानपि प्रेक्ष्य मुदा ननाद |
तेषां समुत्कृष्टरवं निशम्य |
लङ्कालया भीमतरं विनेदुः
verses.iast:
taṃ vānarāḥ prekṣya tadā vineduḥ |
sa tānapi prekṣya mudā nanāda |
teṣāṃ samutkṛṣṭaravaṃ niśamya |
laṇ^kālayā bhīmataraṃ vineduḥ
verses.translation: Then, seeing Hanuma, the monkeys made a noise. Seeing them, Hanuma in turn roared in delight. Hearing their awfully excessive noises the inhabitants of Lanka roared still more terribly.

verses.devanagari:
ततो महात्मा निपपात तस्मिञ् |
शैलोत्तमे वानरसैन्यमध्ये |
हर्युत्तमेभ्यः शिरसाभिवाद्य |
विभीषणं तत्र च सस्वजे सः
verses.iast:
tato mahātmā nipapāta tasmiñ |
śailottame vānarasainyamadhye |
haryuttamebhyaḥ śirasAbhivAdya |
vibhīṣaṇaṃ tatra ca sasvaje saḥ
verses.translation: Thereupon, the great souled Hanuma descended on that prince of mountains (Trikuta) in the midst of that army of monkeys. Having offered salutation to the illustrious monkeys there with his head bent low, he then embraced Vibhishana

glosses.meaning: in the middle of that army of monkeys

verses.devanagari:
तावप्युभौ मानुषराजपुत्रौ |
तं गन्धमाघ्राय महौषधीनाम् |
बभूवतुस्तत्र तदा विशल्या |
उत्तस्थुरन्ये च हरिप्रवीराः
verses.iast:
tāvapyubhau mānuṣarājaputrau |
taṃ gandhamāghrāya mahauṣadhīnām |
babhūvatustatra tadā viśalyā |
uttasthuranye ca haripravīrāḥ
verses.translation: By inhaling that fragrance of those great herbs, both Rama and Lakshamana became healed of their wounds then and there. Other monkey-warriors rose up.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वे विशल्या विरुजाः क्षणेन |
हरिप्रवीराश्च हता श्च ये स्युः |
गन्धेन तासाम् प्रवरौषधीनां |
सुप्ता निशान्तेष्विव संप्रबुद्धाः
verses.iast:
sarve viśalyā virujāḥ kṣaṇena |
haripravīrāśca hatā śca ye syuḥ |
gandhena tāsām pravarauṣadhīnāṃ |
suptā niśānteṣviva samprabuddhāḥ
verses.translation: By the fragrance of those most powerful herbs, all those monkey-warriors who were earlier dead were healed momentarily of their wounds, relieved of their pain, even as those who are asleep fully get up at the close of night.

glosses.meaning: as at the close of night

verses.devanagari:
यदाप्रभृति लङ्कायां युध्यने हरिराक्षसाः |
तदाप्रभृति मानार्थ्माज्ञया रावणस्य च
ये हन्यन्ते रणे तत्र राक्षसाः कपिकुञ्जरैः |
हता हतास्तु क्षिप्यन्ते सर्व एव तु सागरे
verses.iast:
yadāprabhṛti laṇ^kāyāṃ yudhyane harirākṣasāḥ |
tadāprabhṛti mānārthmājJṇayā rāvaṇasya ca
ye hanyante raṇe tatra rākṣasāḥ kapikuJṇjaraiḥ |
hatā hatāstu kṣipyante sarva eva tu sāgare
verses.translation: From the day the monkeys and demons began to fight in Lanka, from that day onwards, under the orders of Ravana, all those demons, who were being killed by the foremost of monkeys were being thrown away into the sea as and when they were killed, merely or the sake of honour (so that their number may not be known to the monkeys).

glosses.meaning: merely for the sake of honour.

verses.devanagari:
ततो हरिर्गन्धवहात्मजस्तु |
तमोषधीशैलमुदग्रवीर्यः |
निनाय वेगाद्धिमवन्तमेव
पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम
verses.iast:
tato harirgandhavahātmajastu |
tamoṣadhīśailamudagravīryaḥ |
nināya vegāddhimavantameva
punaśca rāmeṇa samājagāma
verses.translation: Then, Hanuma the son of wind-god, with a great speed, carried away that mountain of herbs quickly back to the mountains of Himalayas and again joined Rama.

glosses.meaning: whose hair and raiments were kept in order with difficulty
and whose armours and standards were thrown away
